items.title: Stop the first-run tutorial route from visibly collapsing under the reading player
items.premise: The live hosted performance diagnostic for the direct /game.html first-run tutorial path (the exact page a brand-new player sees) already measures desktop CLS 0.4271 and mobile CLS 0.2419 against a 0.1 threshold, plus desktop/mobile LCP 3280ms/2780ms against a 1800ms threshold — all four checks fail in docs/performance/GAME_SHELL_DIAGNOSTIC.json's own evaluation block. The recorded shift sources are five named desktop panels (franchiseCommandCenter, coGmBriefPanel, franchiseArchitecture, trophyRoadPanel, gmCommitmentBoard) and four named mobile elements (overview-hero-side, weeklyPlanSummaryText, footer-guide-panel, game-footer) that render at zero size and then snap to full height once their async content lands, moving the tutorial paragraph the player is mid-reading.
evidence: docs/performance/GAME_SHELL_DIAGNOSTIC.json evaluation.failures: desktop LCP, desktop CLS, mobile LCP, mobile CLS (staging revision 1cfc8774b8f20f2a5bf8951445baadbd6092277a, receipt a9a453beae346fcaf1b040c610f22475bb0eae0508776582c819123750fd8778)
docs/performance/GAME_SHELL_DIAGNOSTIC.json profiles[0].samples[0].shifts naming the five collapsing desktop panel ids
docs/performance/GAME_SHELL_DIAGNOSTIC.json profiles[1].samples[0].shifts naming the four collapsing mobile elements
grep of public/styles.css confirmed no min-height rule exists for franchiseCommandCenter, coGmBriefPanel, franchiseArchitecture, trophyRoadPanel, or gmCommitmentBoard
context/DECISIONS.md D-S82.5: this diagnostic is retained as optimization evidence, not fixed, as of the last closeout
items.constraint: Rendering-order fix only. Do not change the lazy-UI-island hydration contract (D-S73.6), do not add artificial delay, do not change what loads when — only reserve the layout space each panel will occupy once its real content lands, so its arrival stops moving the page.
verification: re-run scripts/measure-hosted-performance.mjs against a staging deploy and confirm desktop and mobile CLS <= 0.1
confirm the recorded LCP element (tutorial-body) and its measured time do not regress further
existing lazy-UI-island and boot-budget tests remain green
dark/light desktop/mobile rendered captures of the tutorial route show no visible flash-then-shift

L1.recipe: Add fixed min-height CSS placeholders sized to typical rendered height for the five desktop panels named in the shift log, matching the existing min-height pattern already used elsewhere in public/styles.css.

L2.recipe: Add min-height reservations for every panel/element named in both the desktop and mobile shift logs at their respective breakpoints, re-run the hosted performance script to prove CLS drops under 0.1 on both profiles, and add a focused test asserting the stylesheet declares a placeholder height for each affected panel id.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a shimmer/skeleton loader matching each panel's final layout so the tutorial route has zero unstyled-content flash in addition to zero shift, proven with dark/light desktop/mobile rendered captures before and after.

items.title: Stop refetching all 32 rival GM personas to render one opponent's Overview card
items.premise: public/lib/tabOverview.js's renderRivalryStrip() calls GET /api/team-archetypes on every Overview render — which fires on essentially every state change (public/app.js:479, 632, 645, 2370, 2373 and public/lib/gameFlow.js:125, covering tab switches, week advances, and sim resolution) — to read exactly one opponent's row. That endpoint (src/app/api/localApiRuntime.js:1719-1729 and the mirrored route in src/server.js:2079) computes buildPersonaIntel() — persona identity plus up to an 8-entry receipted memory ledger — for all 32 league teams every single call, even though only one team's data is ever read from the response at that call site.
evidence: public/lib/tabOverview.js:775-785 fetches `/api/team-archetypes` and reads only `res.archetypes.find(a => a.teamId === opponentId)`
src/app/api/localApiRuntime.js:1722-1729 `archetypes = (session.league.teams || []).map(t => ({ ..., gm: buildPersonaIntel(session.league, t.id) }))` — full 32-team map on every call

public/lib/engagementFeatures.js:615-627 already maintains a separate `_archetypesCache` for the same endpoint's League GM Archetypes table (populated only on demand via the Standings tab's load button), confirming the endpoint has a second, independent full-roster consumer that a scoped param must not break
items.constraint: Keep buildPersonaIntel/getRivalGmPersona as the single shared authority — do not duplicate scoring or persona-generation logic in a new endpoint. The existing full-roster League GM Archetypes table (public/lib/engagementFeatures.js loadTeamArchetypes/renderArchetypesTable) must keep working unchanged.
verification: a single-team-scoped request returns persona/memory/archetype data identical to the matching row of the unscoped response for a sample team
the existing League GM Archetypes table still renders all 32 rows correctly
a focused test measures the scoped response is smaller than the full response for a league with populated grudge memories

L1.recipe: Add an optional `?team=` query param to `/api/team-archetypes` that, when present, computes and returns only that one team's archetype+persona+memory row.

L2.recipe: Add the scoped param on both API adapters (src/app/api/localApiRuntime.js and src/server.js), update tabOverview.js's renderRivalryStrip to request the scoped payload instead of the full roster, and add a focused test proving scoped/unscoped equivalence for the same team.

L3.recipe: L2 plus extend engagementFeatures.js's existing `_archetypesCache` to also store persona/memory, so once the Standings tab has loaded the full roster this session, Overview's rival-intel card reads the warm cache with zero network round trip.

items.title: Add focused coverage for the one browser module that is genuinely untested
items.premise: public/lib/historyFormatting.js exports five pure formatting functions (formatAwardList, hallOfFameCareerLine, awardCountLine, hallOfFamePolicyLine, retiredNumberPolicyLine) consumed by public/lib/tabHistory.js and public/lib/tabSettings.js. After checking three look-alike candidates and finding each already covered (communityEventContract.js via a re-export shim + its own 255-line test, gistCredentials.js via test/gist-sync-security.test.js, pressRoomPanel.js via tests-ui/s63-surfaces.spec.js), this is the one module left with zero references anywhere in test/ or tests-ui/.
evidence: grep across test/ and tests-ui/ for historyFormatting, hallOfFameCareerLine, awardCountLine, hallOfFamePolicyLine, retiredNumberPolicyLine, formatAwardList returns nothing
public/lib/historyFormatting.js:9-14 branches on player position for career-line formatting with no test asserting each position branch (QB/RB/WR-TE/K/P/defense-fallback) produces the right stat line
public/lib/historyFormatting.js:22 sums OROY+DROY+ROY into one displayed 'ROY' count — an easy off-by-composition bug for a future edit to introduce silently without a test catching it
items.constraint: Pure-function unit tests only; no DOM, no snapshot of rendered HTML strings beyond what the functions themselves return.
verification: one test per position branch of hallOfFameCareerLine
awardCountLine's combined ROY count and its zero-value filtering are both asserted
hallOfFamePolicyLine/retiredNumberPolicyLine default and override paths are asserted

L1.recipe: Add tests for hallOfFameCareerLine's six position branches only.

L2.recipe: Add a full focused test file covering all five exports: every position branch, the ROY composition, zero-value award filtering, and both policy-line default/override paths.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a golden-output regression fixture generated from a real simulated Hall of Fame class, so a future stat-shape change to careerStats fails loudly here instead of silently mis-rendering History.

innovationCandidates.novelty: Closes an already-measured, already-recorded CLS/LCP regression on the exact page every new player sees, without re-litigating which route is the canonical release gate.
Scopes an existing full-league persona/memory computation to the single opponent actually rendered, cutting repeated per-render payload and compute without touching the shared persona authority.
Not novel by itself; included because it is the one genuinely uncovered module found after three look-alike candidates were disproven by direct evidence.
